_about: One plain-language sentence per paper, keyed by PubMed ID. Written from the abstract, not the title. Say plainly when work is in animals or cells. If there is no abstract, say so instead of guessing.

papers.42861015: In 66 people with EMAP, a macular condition seen in inherited retinal disease clinics, a sensitivity test of the central retina picked up worsening that standard eye-chart vision missed.
papers.42861385: Describes the gene changes and symptoms of EYS-related RP in 39 patients from Eastern Europe and Northern Asia, and finds two common 'founder' mutations in that population.
papers.42864617: A case series of four siblings with the same CFAP418 gene change, showing that the same mutation can cause quite different symptoms within one family.
papers.42866676: Wide-angle scans of 30 people with USH2A-related RP found changes in the small blood vessels of the outer retina, which were linked to changes in the macula.
papers.42866702: In 106 people with choroideremia followed for a year, the shape of the remaining healthy tissue in the macula helped predict how fast it would shrink.
papers.42877450: A review of efforts to transplant lab-grown retinal tissue made from stem cells, an approach that could someday work regardless of which gene causes RP. It is still mostly at the animal-study stage.
papers.42877765: Lab and animal study: an eye-drop drug candidate called MP-004 reached the retina in mice, rabbits and pigs and looked safe. It has not been tested in people yet.
papers.42877891: A review of the eight retinal and visual prosthesis devices still in development for RP and other blinding conditions, including the ethical questions they raise.
papers.42878232: Lab study using mini-retinas grown from patients' stem cells shows how different CRX gene mutations disrupt developing photoreceptors in LCA7.
papers.42878579: In 74 eyes with RP, the back of the eye flattened where photoreceptors had died, which may explain an unusual eye shape sometimes seen on scans of RP patients.
papers.42881268: A short news article about optogenetic therapy for RP. It is not a research study, and no abstract is available.
papers.42883974: An editorial introducing a journal special issue on the biology of retinal diseases. It contains no new findings.
papers.42884126: Lab study using mini-retinas grown from patients' stem cells points to a fat-processing pathway that may go wrong in RDH12-related LCA.
papers.42887780: Mouse study: after rods and cones die in RP, the next layer of retinal cells keeps working electrical channels. That matters for optogenetic therapies, which rely on those cells.
papers.42890415: Researchers built an AI tool that automatically maps the remaining healthy photoreceptor layer on retinal scans of people with RP, which could make trial measurements faster.
papers.42891053: Animal study: tiny particles released by a type of nerve-support cell helped protect retinal support cells from degeneration when injected under the retina.
papers.42893897: Follows a four-generation family with one dominant CRX mutation and finds that it causes very different severity from person to person.
papers.42897362: Tests machine-learning methods that use an electrical eye test (pattern ERG) to tell apart RP, Stargardt disease and other retinal conditions.
papers.42898535: At a hospital in Türkiye, genetic testing found a clear cause in a substantial share of people with inherited eye diseases, and the study lists which conditions prompted testing.
papers.42899905: Mouse study: a type of copper-driven cell death may contribute to RP, and an existing copper-removing drug injected into the eye slowed degeneration in mice.
papers.42901316: A historical review of major advances in eye care, from cataract lenses to gene therapy.
papers.42904883: A lecture looking back on 40 years of research into the genetics of inherited retinal disease. No abstract is available.
papers.42905171: A German-language review of how Bardet-Biedl syndrome is diagnosed and cared for. It notes there is still no specific treatment for the retinal part of the disease.
papers.42906929: Finds that eye genetics specialists are unevenly spread around the world compared with where people with RP live, leaving many regions underserved.
papers.42909590: Describes 14 Korean patients with IMPG2-related retinal disease and finds that most of their mutations affect how the gene's message is spliced.
papers.42910815: A correction notice for an earlier paper on RPGR and RP. It contains no new findings.
papers.42913796: Pools results from trials of gene therapy injected under the retina in RP. It looks at benefits, effects on retinal structure, and the risks of the surgery itself.
papers.42919695: A review of next-generation ways to override 'stop' mutations, which cause about a fifth of inherited retinal disease. So far these methods have only been tested in the lab.
papers.42923505: A case report of a boy with both Usher syndrome type 2A and a rare form of epilepsy. The authors think the two conditions are probably unrelated.
papers.42923813: Reviews evidence that the eye drops dorzolamide and brinzolamide reduce macular swelling (edema), which is a common, treatable complication of RP.
papers.42924989: Mouse study: in two RP models, calcium pumps in photoreceptors made the inside of the cells more acidic, which helped kill them. This points to a possible target for treatments that work for any gene.
papers.42926372: Preprint, not yet peer-reviewed. In lab and mouse experiments, an engineered protein that calms the retina's immune cells helped preserve cone function in retinal degeneration.
papers.42927157: A case report of a man with fluid-filled bumps under the retina in both eyes plus RP-like loss of rod and cone function.
papers.42927978: Compares 80 U.S. gene therapy trials and finds that injections under the retina have generally worked better than injections into the eye's gel, though they carry surgical risks.
papers.42929859: A review of how artificial intelligence could help develop stem cell and cell therapies for retinal disease, from choosing patients to manufacturing.
papers.42931621: A broad review of what causes RP and of the treatments in development: gene therapy, gene editing, RNA therapies, gene-agnostic approaches and stem cells.
papers.42941794: In 107 Russian patients whose standard genetic test found only one of the two expected mutations, whole-genome sequencing found the missing answer in about 40%.
papers.42941826: Mouse study mapping genes that change how severe photoreceptor loss and eye size are in a model of MFRP-related disease.
papers.42955009: A commentary on the newly reported PRKCZ gene in RP; see the related paper. No abstract is available.
papers.42955015: Identifies PRKCZ as a new gene that causes adult-onset RP when both copies are damaged, which could give answers to some families whose genetic tests came back unsolved.
papers.42957013: Describes the retinal disease and how it changes over time in 12 Japanese patients with NPHP1-related Senior-Løken syndrome, a condition affecting both kidneys and retina.
papers.42957830: A review of laser treatment for children's retinal diseases. RP is mentioned only briefly.
papers.42960537: A case report of a 6-year-old with early-onset retinal dystrophy caused by an NMNAT1 change that standard gene panels miss, showing the value of whole-genome sequencing.
papers.42964045: A correction notice for an earlier paper on genetic testing and family planning. It contains no new findings.
papers.42969949: Lab study showing how the ALMS1 protein, which is faulty in Alström syndrome, keeps cells' antenna-like cilia properly built. Photoreceptors depend on these structures.
papers.42970243: Compares clinical vision tests with people's own sense of how much their vision limits daily life, in a U.K. retinal genetics clinic. The aim is to help trials measure outcomes that matter to patients.
papers.42971418: A technical review of how cell-division signals behave in degenerating retinas.
papers.42972018: Mouse study: a new PDE6B gene therapy design preserved vision and photoreceptors for up to 15 months in a mouse model of PDE6B-related RP.
papers.42972392: A technical review of the structure and signaling of ADGRV1, the gene behind Usher syndrome type 2C.
papers.42977211: Found higher levels of the protein ApoE in the blood of people with RP and, in mice, linked ApoE to inflammation in the retina.
papers.42979557: A review of how animals such as zebrafish regrow retinas, and how those lessons are being turned into vision-restoring treatments, with ratings of how strong the evidence is.
papers.42979679: Reports a new MKKS gene change causing Bardet-Biedl syndrome in an Afghan family.
papers.42980597: Three-year results of a cataract-surgery technique for weak lens support, which is common in RP, with a separate look at RP patients.
papers.42982416: Three case reports linking leaky retinal blood vessels to PRPH2-related macular dystrophy for the first time.
papers.42986169: From the RUSH2A natural history study of USH2A-related RP: overlaying visual field tests on retinal scans could give trials more sensitive ways to measure change.
papers.42986575: Describes seven patients whose CLN-related retinal degeneration was first mistaken for eye inflammation, a reminder to consider genetic causes.
papers.42987996: A letter commenting on an earlier study of lens-power calculations for cataract surgery in RP. No abstract is available.
papers.42990930: No abstract is available yet. The title says it compares gene activity cell by cell across several RP models to find shared responses.
papers.42993231: A clinical update for eye doctors on managing inherited retinal diseases in 2026. No abstract is available.
papers.42995293: Lab study measuring how pig retina stretches and relaxes, to make surgery that injects gene therapy under the retina safer.
papers.43000196: A case series on what happens after a blow to the eye in people with inherited retinal diseases such as Stargardt disease and X-linked retinoschisis.
papers.43003402: A rare case of abnormal blood vessel growth under the retina in a 16-year-old girl who carries a choroideremia gene change.
papers.43004752: Describes TTLL5-related retinal disease in two sisters, aged 14 and 17, in the UAE, showing that it can start in childhood.
papers.43010769: A review, in a Chinese journal, of what affects how well optogenetic therapy (adding a light-sensing gene to surviving retinal cells) might work in RP, such as the condition of the remaining cells, immune reactions to the virus used to deliver it, and when and how it is given. It reports no new patient results.
papers.43014503: A review of AZOOR, a rare and mostly non-inherited condition of the outer retina, which re-examined 207 published cases and found most could now be given a more specific diagnosis using modern eye scans. It is mainly relevant to telling such conditions apart from inherited retinal disease such as RP.
papers.43018415: In 90 people with RP caused by the EYS or USH2A genes, people with exactly the same gene changes often lost vision at very different rates, sometimes with younger people more affected than older ones. The authors say other genes or the environment likely play a part, which matters for predicting how RP will progress and for designing trials.
papers.43018420: In mice, researchers found a new version of the virus used for gene therapy that can reach the retina's support layer (the RPE) from a simple injection into the gel of the eye rather than surgery under the retina; it improved light responses in mice with an RPE65 gene defect (LCA type 2) and reached some of these cells in monkeys. This is early lab work, and the authors note its efficiency is still limited.
papers.43018422: Followed 17 people from eight families with one particular RHO gene change, some for over 20 years, and found it causes a slowly worsening condition that can look like choroideremia rather than typical RP. This may help doctors recognise and counsel families with this variant.
papers.43019019: Found changes in the MYO7A gene, a cause of Usher syndrome type 1 (deafness with RP), in two related-parent families in Pakistan with hearing loss and vision problems; one of the changes has not been reported before. The work gives these families a genetic diagnosis.
papers.43020825: In a mouse model of X-linked RP (RPGR gene) and in lab-grown cells, researchers found a stress response inside cells, linked to lower levels of a protein called Cryaa, that contributes to the death of light-sensing cells. This is lab work that may point to new treatment ideas, not a treatment.
papers.43021544: In mice with a mild form of Zellweger spectrum disorder, a rare whole-body condition that also damages the retina, a one-time gene therapy injected under the retina protected vision and retinal structure for 6 months. This is animal work only.
papers.43022838: Researchers used genome testing to find hidden gene changes in SDCCAG8, CEP290 and ABCA4 in patients with inherited retinal disease, then designed small RNA-based drugs (antisense oligonucleotides) that partly corrected the faulty gene reading in patients' skin cells and lab-grown retinal tissue. This is lab work; none were tested in people.
